title: Atomic Structure and Spectroscopy
question: How can a calibrated spectrum constrain an atomic-structure model?
summary: Relate hydrogen-like energy levels and transitions to wavelength and frequency under a stated Hamiltonian. Line identification, calibration, selection rules, broadening assumptions, reduced mass, and competing-model checks constrain inference; a spectrum does not reveal a unique atomic structure by inspection, and dimensional combinations cannot replace a bound-state model.

caveats: Spectral inference is model- and calibration-dependent.
